scope: Calibration of dialog entry, counts and hints, not independent generalization. The existing verifier withholds dialog inputs: first lexical matches are diagnostics, not verified accuracy. Static authored inputs and both predictions fixed before Native; no speech-engine changes until both profiles finish. Native AX scope names and target geometry independently checked. Expected direct-child counts are preregistered structural hypotheses, not labels inferred from speech. Raw receipts/first predictions/failures immutable. No Navigation/State/Task accuracy or native speech-completion claim.

plan.question: How do nonmodal dialog names, direct exposed children, anonymous wrappers, native dialog markup and singleton counts affect entry, within-dialog and reverse-return speech in Safari and Chrome? Five controlled contrasts, no navigation simulation.
plan.hypothesis: Dialog prefix/hint words may differ by browser; Safari may announce dialog context on within-dialog focus. Native direct-child count and immediate exposed parent may explain counts and hint locations. Current dialog input verifier remains unsupported; preserve this first measurement gap and diagnostic wording separately.
plan.inputPolicy: Authored DOM supplies static target/default semantics and expected dialog AX name/direct-child count; independently verify role/name/state/ancestor scopes and visible target geometry after each action. Expected counts are a preregistered structural hypothesis, not a count inferred from the utterance. Actual Native child structure and immediate parent must be archived for later independent calibration. Unused counts are placeholders. A mismatch stays a mismatch.
plan.attribution: Existing bounded receipt-window quality gate; no native completion guarantee. Collect both browsers before changes. All planned rows preserved. Calibration, not independent accuracy or Navigation/State/Task Success.
